shortSummary: Cauliflorous tropical evergreen bearing the largest tree-borne syncarp fruit in the world—celebrated as Bangladesh's national fruit.
leadOverview: Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus), known affectionately across Bengal as Kathal and honoured as the national fruit of Bangladesh, is a stout evergreen tree in the mulberry-fig family (Moraceae). Capable of yielding massive cauliflorous compound fruits weighing over 35 kilograms straight off sturdy trunks, it delivers both sweet golden arils and high-protein young vegetable flesh.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Cauliflory, heterophyllous leaves, milky latex, and gigantic hexagonal syncarps
sections.summary: Anatomy of lobed-to-entire leaves, unisexual spikes, and massive multiple fruits.
paragraphs: Artocarpus heterophyllus develops a dense conical-to-domed evergreen crown 10 to 25 metres tall, bearing thick, dark grey-brown bark and abundant sticky white latex throughout every tissue. Its specific epithet heterophyllus ('varied-leaf') describes the dramatic contrast between juvenile three-lobed shoots and mature, glossy, leathery dark-green elliptic leaves.

Monoecious trees produce separate male and female dense cylindrical flower spikes (inflorescences) emerging directly on the main trunk and stout interior limbs—a trait called cauliflory suited to heavy fruit loads. Pollinated female spikes swell into colossal multiple fruits (syncarps) covered in blunt hexagonal tubercles, enclosing dozens of fleshy golden perianth bulbs (arils) around starchy seeds.

subblocks.heading: Cauliflorous Trunk
subblocks.text: Thick woody trunks and scaffold boughs bearing short fruit stalks capable of supporting 15–40 kg syncarps.

subblocks.heading: Heterophyllous Leaves
subblocks.text: Lobed saplings transitioning into glossy oblong-obovate mature blades (10–20 cm) with pale central midribs.

subblocks.heading: Unisexual Spikes
subblocks.text: Drooping green male catkins (shedding clouds of pollen) paired with stout oblong female spikes.

subblocks.heading: Syncarp Fruit & Roots
subblocks.text: World's largest tree fruit enclosing sweet golden bulbs and large starchy seeds; deep moisture-seeking taproot.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Rosales order and Moraceae breadfruit kinship
sections.summary: Relationship with breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis), cempedak, and figs in Moraceae.
paragraphs: Assigned to order Rosales and family Moraceae, Artocarpus heterophyllus shares milky laticifers and aggregate syncarp fruits with Pacific breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis), marang, and Southeast Asian cempedak (Artocarpus integer).

Horticulturists classify jackfruit landraces into two primary texture types: firm-fleshed crisp types ('Khaja' or 'Varka') preferred for fresh dessert segments, and soft, aromatic, melting-pulp types ('Gala' or 'Koozha') ideal for nectars and preserves.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: Humid monsoon foothills and Madhupur terrace orchards of Bangladesh
sections.summary: From ancient Western Ghats rainforests to homestead agroforestry across the tropics.
paragraphs: Botanical consensus traces wild Artocarpus heterophyllus to the humid evergreen and semi-evergreen rainforests of southwestern India's Western Ghats, spreading millennia ago across eastern Bengal, Myanmar, and Maritime Southeast Asia. It thrives in deep, well-drained alluvial or red lateritic soils up to 1,200 metres elevation.

In Bangladesh—especially across the undulating red terrace uplands of Gazipur, Madhupur, and Tangail—jackfruit serves as a quintessential homestead tree tolerant of hot monsoon summers yet requiring drainage above seasonal flood levels.

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Wind-plus-beetle pollination and megafaunal seed dispersal
sections.summary: Sap-feeding nitidulid beetles, wind pollen, and wildlife frugivore networks.
paragraphs: Jackfruit combines anemophily (wind-borne pollen clouds from fragrant male spikes) with entomophily mediated by tiny gall midges and sap-feeding nitidulid beetles attracted to banana-scented volatiles emitted during receptive bloom.

In native forest ecosystems, aromatic fallen syncarps feed elephants, deer, monkeys, civets, and wild pigs that disperse intact starchy seeds across forest clearings, while dense canopies host nesting birds.

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: National fruit of Bangladesh, vegan shredded meat, and golden woodworking timber
sections.summary: Zero-waste utility spanning ripe fruit, unripe vegetable curries, roasted seeds, and durable timber.
paragraphs: Honoured as Bangladesh's national fruit, jackfruit delivers astonishing zero-waste value: unripe green fruits (echor) possess fibrous neutral flesh prized globally as a plant-based pulled-meat substitute in biryanis, curries, and tacos; ripe honey-sweet bulbs flavour cakes and smoothies; and boiled or roasted seeds taste remarkably like chestnuts.

Beyond food, fallen leaves feed goats during dry winters, and golden-yellow heartwood (rich in morin pigment) is prized across South Asia for fine furniture, doors, and classical stringed musical instruments such as the veena and mridangam.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Artocarpin, jacalin lectin, carotenoids, and prebiotic seed starch
sections.summary: Rich potassium-and-phytonutrient profile alongside latex and birch-pollen allergy notes.
paragraphs: Ripe jackfruit provides substantial vitamin C, potassium, dietary fibre, and beta-carotene, while seeds contain resistant prebiotic starches and jacalin—a galactose-binding lectin extensively utilized in immunology laboratories worldwide to purify human IgA antibodies.
Heartwood and root flavonoids including artocarpin and cyanomaclurin demonstrate notable antioxidant and antibacterial effects in preclinical research.
sections.safetyNote: Sticky latex inside unripe fruit can trigger skin sensitization or cross-reactive oral allergy syndrome in individuals allergic to natural rubber latex or birch pollen; oiling knives and hands before cutting prevents contact irritation, and people with chronic kidney disease should monitor high potassium intake.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Flood intolerance, fresh seed sowing, bud-grafting, and fruit thinning
sections.summary: Establishing healthy grafted orchards with strong drainage and scaffold pruning.
paragraphs: Unlike mango or coconut, jackfruit roots perish rapidly under prolonged waterlogging; always plant on raised terraces, gentle slopes, or deep well-drained sandy-loam hills (pH 6.0–7.5) in frost-free full sun. Sow fresh recalcitrant seeds immediately in deep bags, or plant cleft-grafted saplings for early 3-year fruiting.

Maintain clear interior scaffold branches so pollinators and sunlight reach trunk-borne flower spikes, thin excess clusters to 1 or 2 fruits per node for uniform size, and harvest once tapping the rind emits a hollow, dull thud.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Spring (বসন্ত), Summer (গ্রীষ্ম)).
paragraphs: Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Spring (বসন্ত), Summer (গ্রীষ্ম).

Spring (বসন্ত): Cauliflorous male and female inflorescence spikes ('মুচি') emerge directly along thick trunks and main limbs. Summer (গ্রীষ্ম): Giant prickly syncarps swell and ripen fragrant golden bulbs across Gazipur and Madhupur terraces.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for Jackfruit.
paragraphs: Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) combines sexual seed propagation—useful for raising sturdy heterozygous rootstocks—with elite clonal techniques such as veneer grafting, air layering (gootee), and semi-hardwood stem cuttings. Fresh recalcitrant or semi-orthodox seeds typically germinate within 14 to 35 days when depulped and sown in warm organic loam.
Clonal orchards standardize crown architecture, early precocity, and uniform biochemical profiles across generations within Moraceae.

subblocks.heading: Nursery Seed Protocol
subblocks.text: Depulped seed sown cleanly in 2:1 loam-compost media; high viability when fresh.

subblocks.heading: Clonal Method
subblocks.text: Approach/veneer grafting or monsoon air-layering onto vigorous local rootstocks.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Artocarpus heterophyllus.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of Jackfruit.
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (South & Southeast Asia (Western Ghats & Indo-Bengal)), Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

subblocks.heading: Ecological Resilience
subblocks.text: Adapted to South & Southeast Asia (Western Ghats & Indo-Bengal) thermal oscillations and seasonal hydrological extremes.

subblocks.heading: Stewardship Strategy
subblocks.text: Preserve traditional landraces, pollinator corridors, and living herbarium voucher plots.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 6.0 – 7.2 (Slightly acidic to neutral), Full Sun to Partial Filtered Light (6+ hrs), and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 6.0 – 7.2 (Slightly acidic to neutral) inside well-drained organic sandy-clay loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across full sun to partial filtered light (6+ hrs).

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate deep watering scaled to monsoon rhythm) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Rosales clade divergence and Moraceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Artocarpus within order Rosales (Eudicot (Fabids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Artocarpus heterophyllus inside family Moraceae (মোরাসি (ডুমুর-কাঁঠাল গোত্র)), order Rosales, clade Eudicot (Fabids). Laticiferous tropical canopy giants producing milky latex and remarkable multiple fruits—ranging from inverted fig syconia to cauliflorous jackfruit syncarps.

Within genus Artocarpus, specialized morphological adaptations—such as abundant white milky latex across bark, petioles, and fruit—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Artocarpus heterophyllus (Kathal (কাঁঠাল)).
paragraphs: Field verification of Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) rests on recognizing key Moraceae family markers: Abundant white milky latex across bark, petioles, and fruit; Conical sheathing stipules leaving circular scars on twigs; Compound multiple fruits (syconia or trunk-borne syncarps). Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.
